turns.question: There are no king cobra records inside EBTL. Can they still be there? Please use records from nearby areas to make a careful estimate.
turns.answer:
Yes, they still could be there, but I would treat it as **possible and probably rare**, not likely/common.

What I found:
- EBTL is in the **Krishnagiri-Melagiri foothill landscape** in Tamil Nadu, not an isolated site. Public EBTL pages place it near Budhimutlu in the eastern edge of the **Bilgiri-Melagiri hill complex**. Source: [EBTL site](https://ebtl.earth/), [research page](https://ebtl.earth/cegs/).
- A 2018 public herpetofauna survey of the **Bilgiri-Melagiri massif and other Southern Eastern Ghats sites** recorded 37 snake species, but I did **not** find king cobra listed in that survey. Source: [Ganesh et al. 2018](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331523059_Herpetofauna_of_Southern_Eastern_Ghats_India-II_From_Western_Ghats_to_Coromandel_Coast).
- Public citizen-science checklists I found for **Krishnagiri** and **Melagiris** also did **not** show king cobra records. Sources: [Krishnagiri checklist](https://www.inaturalist.org/check_lists/316682-Krishnagiri-Check-List), [Melagiris checklist](https://www.inaturalist.org/check_lists/4104133-Melagiris-Check-List).
- But king cobra is publicly recorded from **Tamil Nadu** and from the **Eastern Ghats more broadly**. Sources: [India Biodiversity Portal](https://indiabiodiversity.org/species/show/238894), [Eastern Ghats Wildlife Society](https://eghats.org/home/program/king-cobra-conservation), [Indian Reptiles](https://www.indianreptiles.org/ophiophagus-hannah).

My estimate:
- **Inside EBTL itself:** possible, but I would guess **low probability at present**.
- **In the wider nearby hill forest landscape:** more plausible, especially in **better forested, wetter, less disturbed patches** than the EBTL valley floor.
- So the most careful wording is: **“No confirmed public record inside EBTL, but occasional presence in the surrounding landscape is still biologically plausible.”**

What is missing:
- No verified public record I found from **inside EBTL**.
- No clear georeferenced public king cobra record from the **immediate Krishnagiri/Melagiri-EBTL vicinity**.
- No local systematic snake survey, rescue log, or repeated night transects focused on king cobra habitat around EBTL.

If useful, I can next turn this into a **2-3 sentence NGO-ready note** or a **simple confidence table**.

turns.question: Why did you accept or reject this estimate?
turns.answer:
I would **accept the estimate only in a cautious form**:

**Accepted:** “King cobras could still occur in or near EBTL, but probably rarely.”
**Rejected:** “King cobras are likely/common in EBTL” or “they are definitely absent.”

Why I accepted the cautious estimate:
- **EBTL is connected to a larger hill-forest landscape**, not an isolated site, so absence of records does not prove absence. Source: [EBTL](https://ebtl.earth/), [CEGS at EBTL](https://ebtl.earth/cegs/).
- **King cobra is known from Tamil Nadu and the Eastern Ghats region**, so the species is not impossible there. Sources: [India Biodiversity Portal](https://indiabiodiversity.org/species/show/238894), [Eastern Ghats Wildlife Society](https://eghats.org/home/program/king-cobra-conservation), [Indian Reptiles](https://www.indianreptiles.org/ophiophagus-hannah).
- **No record inside EBTL is not strong evidence of absence**, especially for a rare, hard-to-detect snake.

Why I rejected a stronger estimate:
- A public **Southern Eastern Ghats herpetofauna survey** did not clearly show king cobra from the Melagiri-side area I checked. Source: [Ganesh et al. 2018](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331523059_Herpetofauna_of_Southern_Eastern_Ghats_India-II_From_Western_Ghats_to_Coromandel_Coast).
- Public **Krishnagiri** and **Melagiris** checklists I found also did not show king cobra records. Sources: [Krishnagiri checklist](https://www.inaturalist.org/check_lists/316682-Krishnagiri-Check-List), [Melagiris checklist](https://www.inaturalist.org/check_lists/4104133-Melagiris-Check-List).
- So there is **not enough public evidence** to say they are definitely present in EBTL.

What is missing:
- A verified **record from inside EBTL**
- **Georeferenced nearby records** from the immediate EBTL surroundings
- A **systematic local survey** or rescue log

So, in simple terms: I accepted a **possible but rare** estimate because the wider landscape makes presence plausible, and I rejected any **stronger claim** because the public local evidence is still weak.

turns.question: What is the biggest doubt in this estimate? What should our field team check at EBTL?
turns.answer:
The **biggest doubt** is whether habitat at **EBTL itself** is suitable for king cobra, not just whether the wider region is. Public sources suggest the larger **Bilgiri-Melagiri / Eastern Ghats landscape** can support the species, but I did **not** find a verified public record from inside EBTL or its immediate surroundings. Sources: [EBTL](https://ebtl.earth/), [Ganesh et al. 2018](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331523059_Herpetofauna_of_Southern_Eastern_Ghats_India-II_From_Western_Ghats_to_Coromandel_Coast), [India Biodiversity Portal](https://indiabiodiversity.org/species/show/238894).

What the field team should check at EBTL:
- Look for **good king cobra habitat**: moist forest patches, shaded stream lines, dense cover, low disturbance.
- Check whether there are **many other snakes**, especially rat snakes and other forest snakes, because king cobras feed mainly on snakes.
- Ask for and verify any **direct evidence**: photos, shed skins, roadkills, rescue records, camera-trap bycatch, or reliable sightings from staff and nearby communities.
- Search likely areas in the **wet season and early morning**, especially along streams, forest edges, and less-disturbed slopes.

What I found:
- The region is connected to a larger forested hill system, so presence is **possible**.
- I found **no public confirmed record inside EBTL**.

What I estimate:
- If EBTL still has suitable moist forest and enough prey snakes, king cobra presence is **possible but probably rare**.

What is missing:
- A **verified EBTL record**
- **Georeferenced nearby records**
- A **systematic local survey** focused on large forest snakes

A simple NGO-safe answer would be: **“The main uncertainty is whether EBTL itself has the right habitat and prey base. Our field team should first check moist forest patches, stream lines, snake abundance, and any direct local evidence.”**
